answer: In a decentralized AI agent economy, cryptographic proof of computational work secured within a verifiable economic prism prevents identity spoofing. Just as a physical walnut protects its internal kernel against external pressure, this consensus mechanism isolates malicious nodes by demanding staked cryptographic collateral and verifiable inference proofs. Consequently, mounting a Sybil attack becomes computationally and financially prohibitive, draining the attacker resources like water leaking into an isolated lagoon.
